criterion.title: Identify Oversized Files
criterion.goal: Scan codebase and identify all files >1000 lines
criterion.technicalApproach: - Use find command to scan raglite/ directory for .py files - Create script: scripts/identify-oversized-files.py with standardized report format - Report format: File Path | Line Count | Epic 3 Relevance | Priority

criterion.title: Define Refactoring Strategy
criterion.goal: Plan how to split oversized modules by domain/responsibility
criterion.technicalApproach: - For each oversized file: identify logical boundaries (domain separation) - Define new module names (maintain single responsibility) - Plan import updates - Example: Split 1500-line query_classifier into entity_matching, period_mapping, sql_generation, classifier modules
criterion.successCriteria: - Refactoring plan documented for each oversized file - New module boundaries defined (single responsibility principle) - Winston architecture review approves strategy - Validation: Winston approval documented in docs/refactoring/winston-approval-3.0.1.md - Files Created: docs/refactoring/refactoring-strategy.md

criterion.title: Execute Refactoring
criterion.goal: Split oversized modules and maintain 100% test coverage
criterion.technicalApproach: - For each file: create new focused modules, move functions/classes, update imports - Safety protocol: one file at a time, full test suite after each refactor, commit after success - Refactoring checklist per file: create modules, move code, update imports, run pytest, check coverage
criterion.successCriteria: - All files <1000 lines - 100% test pass rate maintained (no regressions) - Test coverage maintained: pytest --cov=raglite ≥ baseline established at story start - Integration tests pass: pytest tests/integration/ - Code functionality unchanged (refactor only, no features) - Test Failure Protocol: If pytest fails → rollback, debug, retry using pytest --exitfirst - Performance Check (Optional): Test suite runtime unchanged (within ±10% of baseline)

doc.title: Epic 3: AI Intelligence & Orchestration
doc.snippet: Epic goal: Enable multi-step reasoning and complex analytical workflows through agentic orchestration. This epic builds on Epic 1-2's retrieval foundation and requires clean, maintainable codebase for agentic features.

doc.title: Epic 3 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Epic 3 adds orchestration layer (~280 lines) to monolithic structure. Agents are simple Python async functions (~50 lines each), maintaining simplicity-first philosophy. Clean module boundaries enable multi-agent coordination.

doc.title: RAGLite Coding Standards
doc.snippet: MANDATORY: Type hints, Google-style docstrings, structured logging, async/await for I/O. Module size enforcement: ⚠️ Warning at 800 lines, ❌ Error at 1000 lines, 🎯 Target 200-400 lines per file.

doc.title: Repository Structure (Monolithic)
doc.snippet: Target: ~600-800 lines total across 15 files. Each module focused on single responsibility: ingestion (~150 lines), retrieval (~150 lines), shared (~100 lines). Maintainability through focused modules.

doc.title: Epic 2 Retrospective
doc.snippet: Action Item 2: Ricardo identified files exceeding 1000-1500 lines as technical debt. Proposal: Enforce module size limits (hard stop at 1000 lines) in architecture review checklist to prevent future violations.

interface.name: Refactoring Module Pattern
interface.signature:
# Split large module into focused sub-modules original_module/ large_file.py (2300 lines) →
original_module/ core.py (400 lines - orchestrator) domain_a.py (300 lines - focused logic) domain_b.py (500 lines - focused logic) utils.py (200 lines - helpers)

interface.name: Import Update Pattern
interface.signature:
# After splitting modules, update imports across codebase # Old: from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import function_x # New: from raglite.ingestion.core import function_x
# Use IDE refactoring tools or grep to find all references grep -r "from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import" raglite/

interface.name: Test Validation Pattern
interface.signature: # After each refactor: 1. Run pytest (verify all tests pass) 2. Run pytest --cov (verify coverage maintained) 3. Run pytest tests/integration/ (verify integration tests pass) 4. Commit changes (rollback safety)

interface.name: Test Import Update Pattern
interface.signature:
# Automated import update workflow:
# Step 1: Create import mapping (before refactoring) import_mapping = { "from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import ingest_pdf": "from raglite.ingestion.pdf_ingestion import ingest_pdf", "from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import chunk_document": "from raglite.ingestion.chunking import chunk_document", # ... map all imports }
# Step 2: Use compatibility shim during transition # raglite/ingestion/pipeline.py (temporary) from .pdf_ingestion import ingest_pdf from .chunking import chunk_document __all__ = ['ingest_pdf', 'chunk_document', ...]
# Step 3: Run automated import update script python scripts/update_test_imports.py --dry-run # Preview python scripts/update_test_imports.py --apply # Apply
# Step 4: Verify imports pytest tests/ --collect-only # Test discovery works pytest tests/ -x # Run tests, stop on first failure
interface.path: Deep analysis findings - Test management protocol

interface.name: Pre-Refactoring Baseline Pattern
interface.signature:
# CRITICAL: Run BEFORE any refactoring begins
# 1. Record baseline test results pytest tests/ -v --tb=short > baseline_test_results.txt
# 2. Record baseline coverage pytest --cov=raglite --cov-report=term > baseline_coverage.txt
# 3. Record test execution time time pytest tests/ | tee baseline_timing.txt
# 4. Create test dependency mapping grep -r "from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import" tests/ > test_dependencies_pipeline.txt grep -r "from raglite.ingestion.adaptive_table_extraction import" tests/ > test_dependencies_table.txt
# 5. Git checkpoint git add -A git commit -m "checkpoint: pre-refactoring baseline"

interface.name: Module Split with Test Safety Pattern
interface.signature:
# For EACH oversized module being split:
# Phase 1: Split module CODE (keep compatibility) 1. Create new focused modules (e.g., pdf_ingestion.py, chunking.py) 2. Move functions to appropriate modules 3. Add re-exports to original module (compatibility shim): from .pdf_ingestion import ingest_pdf __all__ = ['ingest_pdf', ...]
# Phase 2: Verify compatibility shim works 4. Run affected unit tests: pytest tests/unit/test_ingestion.py -v 5. Run affected integration tests: pytest tests/integration/ -k ingestion 6. STOP if any failures - fix before continuing
# Phase 3: Update test imports (optional, can defer) 7. Update test files to import from new modules directly 8. Run import update script: python scripts/update_test_imports.py --module pipeline 9. Verify: pytest tests/ --collect-only (test discovery)
# Phase 4: Full validation 10. Run full suite: pytest tests/ 11. Check coverage: pytest --cov=raglite.ingestion 12. Compare to baseline (no regression)
# Phase 5: Commit 13. git add -A 14. git commit -m "refactor: split pipeline.py into focused modules"

tests.standards:
All refactoring changes must maintain 100% test pass rate. Testing framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio for async functions. Test organization follows consolidated structure in tests/ directory (unit/, integration/, e2e/). Coverage target: maintain baseline established at story start (use pytest --cov=raglite). Test naming: test_<module>_<function>_<scenario>.py. Run tests after EVERY module split using: uv run pytest (fast tests), uv run pytest tests/integration/ (integration validation). Use pytest --exitfirst for immediate failure detection during refactoring.
CRITICAL TEST MANAGEMENT REQUIREMENTS: - 12 test files depend on pipeline.py (9 import ingest_pdf, 5 import chunk_document) - 1 test file depends on adaptive_table_extraction.py - MUST establish baseline BEFORE refactoring (test results, coverage, timing, dependencies) - MUST use compatibility shims (re-export pattern) to avoid breaking tests during transition - MUST use automated import update scripts (NO manual updates - too error-prone) - Test discovery validation required after each module split (pytest --collect-only) - Per-module validation gates: run affected tests before full suite - Fixture compatibility verification (tests/conftest.py may need updates) - Final validation: 100% test pass (358/358), coverage ≥ baseline, timing within ±10%
tests.locations: tests/unit/ - Unit tests for all modules (~200 tests, no external dependencies) tests/integration/ - Integration tests with Qdrant/PostgreSQL (~115 tests) tests/e2e/ - End-to-end tests (~28 tests) tests/conftest.py - Shared pytest fixtures tests/ground_truth.json - Accuracy validation test set (50+ Q&A pairs)

test-idea.approach: MUST RUN BEFORE ANY REFACTORING: 1. pytest tests/ -v --tb=short > baseline_test_results.txt 2. pytest --cov=raglite --cov-report=term > baseline_coverage.txt 3. time pytest tests/ | tee baseline_timing.txt 4. grep -r "from raglite.ingestion.pipeline import" tests/ > test_dependencies_pipeline.txt 5. grep -r "from raglite.ingestion.adaptive_table_extraction import" tests/ > test_dependencies_table.txt 6. git commit -m "checkpoint: pre-refactoring baseline"
Test scripts/identify-oversized-files.py output format and accuracy. Mock file system with known files >1000 lines. Verify report includes file path, line count, priority.

For each oversized module being split, create comprehensive import mapping: - Map old imports to new module locations - Document which test files need updates - Create scripts/import_mapping.json with complete mapping - Validate mapping covers all 12 test files for pipeline.py

For each split module, create re-export compatibility layer: - Original module (e.g., pipeline.py) becomes re-export shim - Import all functions from new modules - Use __all__ to explicitly list exports - Run pytest tests/ to verify shim works - Keep shim until all tests updated (can defer removal)

Create and run scripts/update_test_imports.py: 1. Dry run: python scripts/update_test_imports.py --dry-run 2. Review changes for accuracy 3. Apply: python scripts/update_test_imports.py --apply 4. Verify: pytest tests/ --collect-only (test discovery) 5. Run tests: pytest tests/ -x (stop on first failure)

After EACH module split: 1. Run affected unit tests first: pytest tests/unit/test_[module].py -v 2. Run affected integration tests: pytest tests/integration/ -k [module] 3. STOP if failures, fix before continuing 4. Run full suite: pytest tests/ 5. Check coverage: pytest --cov=raglite.[module_path] 6. Compare to baseline (no regression allowed)

After import updates, verify test discovery: - pytest --collect-only (should find all 358 tests) - pytest --collect-only tests/unit/ (verify unit tests discovered) - pytest --collect-only tests/integration/ (verify integration tests discovered) - No "import errors" or "collection errors" allowed

Establish baseline coverage before refactoring: pytest --cov=raglite --cov-report=term > baseline_coverage.txt. After each refactor: pytest --cov=raglite --cov-report=term > current_coverage.txt. Compare coverage percentages - should not decrease. Pay special attention to ingestion module coverage.

Run full integration suite after each major refactor: pytest tests/integration/ -v. Critical tests: test_ac3_ground_truth.py (77.6% accuracy maintained), test_sql_routing.py (SQL table search functional), test_hybrid_search.py (BM25 + semantic search working), test_ingestion_integration.py (full pipeline works).

Verify shared fixtures still work after module splits: - Check tests/conftest.py for fixtures using refactored modules - Run tests using those fixtures: pytest tests/ -v -k fixture_name - Update fixture imports if needed (rare, most fixtures are in conftest.py)
Optional but recommended: Install pydeps (pip install pydeps), run pydeps raglite --max-bacon=2 to generate dependency graph. Verify no circular imports between newly created modules.

Create validation script: scripts/validate-module-sizes.py. Run after refactoring complete. Script checks: no file >1000 lines (hard fail), files near 800 lines flagged as warnings. Exit code 1 if violations found.

Compare final results to pre-refactoring baseline: - Test pass rate: Must be 100% (358/358 tests passing) - Coverage: Must be ≥ baseline percentage - Timing: Should be within ±10% of baseline - All import errors resolved - No test discovery issues - Document any acceptable deviations
